turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Finn and Mum? I'm one of the healthcare assistants. Before you see the doctor, his temperature was thirty six point eight, pulse a hundred and twelve, breathing twenty six, oxygen ninety eight percent, and he weighed fourteen point two kilos.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thanks. We've barely slept, so if I muddle the story that's why.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): You're fine. Room two whenever you're ready, he knows you're here.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, come on in. I'm Dr Shah. What's brought Finn down today?
[SEG0005] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's his ear, really. He's been crying in the night and tugging at the right one. It came on after a cold.
[SEG0006] person_4 (PATIENT): My ear hurts. I don't like it.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry, Finn. Which ear is the sore one?
[SEG0008] person_4 (PATIENT): This one. The right. Will you hurt me?
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll only look with a little light, it shouldn't hurt. Mum, how long has it been sore?
[SEG0010] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): About a week— no, sorry, three days. Monday night was the first bad one. I'm getting my days mixed.
[SEG0011] person_4 (PATIENT): Am I poorly?
[SEG0012] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A bit, love, he's only three. He's been screaming with it after bedtime for two nights, and last night he wouldn't settle till gone three.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has he had a fever at all with this?
[SEG0014] person_4 (PATIENT): I was hot. Gran said.

[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, I don't think he has. Gran had her hand on him and said he was burning, but his forehead was cool when I felt it. We've no thermometer at home. He wasn't feverish.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): So there's no number from home. You didn't find a fever, and he says he felt hot, and in clinic today he's thirty six point eight, which is normal.
[SEG0017] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, that's fair. I still say no fever.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any gunk or discharge coming out of the ear?
[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's gone off his food. He only wanted a bit of toast this morning.
[SEG0020] person_4 (PATIENT): I want to go home.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): In a minute, Finn. Mum, was anything actually leaking from the ear?
[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh, no, nothing leaking. Sorry, I went off somewhere else.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting or diarrhoea?
[SEG0024] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting and no diarrhoea. Wees are fine. He's drinking, he's just not eating much.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the cough, the cold, his breathing?
[SEG0026] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Snotty cold last week, mostly gone. Still a bit of a dry cough, not chesty. No wheeze. He's not breathless.
[SEG0027] person_4 (PATIENT): Can I go to nursery? I miss painting.
[SEG0028] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's tomorrow, we'll ask. Doctor, is the cough part of this or something separate?
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Often it's the same virus. Let me have a look in the ears first, Finn, just the light.
[SEG0030] person_4 (PATIENT): I don't want the light. Will it hurt?

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): It won't hurt. The right eardrum is red and a bit dull, with no hole in it, and the left ear looks clear. Throat's mildly pink, the chest is clear, and there's no tenderness behind the ear.
[SEG0032] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So is it an infection? Does he need antibiotics? I really don't want to give him something if it'll make him rashy.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has he reacted to an antibiotic before?
[SEG0034] person_4 (PATIENT): Medicine is yucky.

[SEG0035] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): When he was little he had penicillin— no, it was amoxicillin, the sweet one, and he got a rash, maybe. It might have just been the virus, I was never sure. It was long ago, and I can't tell you when, whether he was a baby or already walking, I've lost track.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): So a possible rash with amoxicillin, not a definite allergy, and you can't date it. Anything else he reacts to, medicines or foods?
[SEG0037] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nothing else that I know of. No food allergies. I'm just nervous about the amoxicillin.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Understood, we'll keep off it. What have you given him for the pain?

[SEG0039] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Calpol, the infant one, a hundred and twenty milligrams in five mils. I gave five mils— no, seven and a half mils, I keep forgetting he's on the bigger dose now. Bedtime and again about two in the morning, the last two nights.
[SEG0040] person_4 (PATIENT): Do I have to take more medicine? I won't.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Maybe, we'll see. Any asthma, eczema, or trips into hospital?

[SEG0042] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No asthma, no eczema. Never been in hospital. His dad had loads of ear infections as a boy, if that matters. We live with— well, he lives with me, and my mum helps most days.

[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me put it together: three days of right ear pain, worse at night with crying, after a cold that's mostly settled, with a bit of dry cough left, eating less but drinking fine, and no discharge, vomiting, diarrhoea or wheeze. Fever isn't confirmed, because you think he hasn't had one and he says he felt hot. The right drum is red and dull, which fits a mild middle ear infection after the virus. I think that's what this is, and a lot of these settle without antibiotics.
[SEG0044] person_4 (PATIENT): Is it going to come back? I'm scared.
[SEG0045] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So what do we do, just wait? What if tonight is awful again? Should I wake him for Calpol, and can he go to nursery tomorrow?

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Watch and wait is reasonable, he's well in himself. Keep the Calpol going, seven and a half mils up to four times a day if he needs it, including in the night if he's awake and sore, but don't wake him just for a dose. Nursery is fine if he's comfortable and not feverish, and if he's miserable keep him home.
[SEG0047] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if it doesn't settle?

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll write a back-up prescription for clarithromycin, not amoxicillin. For his weight, seventy five— no, a hundred and five milligrams twice a day, for five days. Don't start it today. Only start it if he's no better in three days, or if he becomes more poorly or a fever shows up.
[SEG0049] person_4 (PATIENT): Will that one taste bad?
[SEG0050] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is clarithromycin safe if that amoxicillin rash was real? And would I start it on Friday?

[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the rash was a true allergy it would be to the penicillin family, and clarithromycin is a different group, so that's the one we'd use. Start it only if by three days he's still in a lot of pain, or sooner if he gets a fever, is very drowsy, stops drinking, or you see swelling behind the ear. Otherwise don't use it.
[SEG0052] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. Do I need to come back as well, or only if he's not right?

[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): If he's not better in three days, book back in and we'll see him again, whether or not you've started the medicine. If he worsens before that, don't wait, come back or call us the same day.
[SEG0054] person_4 (PATIENT): Can I have a sticker if I'm brave? I want to go home.

[SEG0055] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Stickers are at my desk, Finn. Mum, the back-up script will be on the system if you end up needing it, just ask us, and we'll fit a review in if the three days pass and he's still sore.
